decisions.reason: The verb is to ask for the return of something lent (meaning decision m3). "Kudai" is to claim what is owed, so it keeps the picture of a loan called in; Literal keeps the indefinite "they" (m2), and Balanced the passive, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "phán" for God speaking, and "ngươi" for the man he rebukes
decisions.reason: "phán" is kept for God speaking (style guide). God speaks to the fool as judge; "ngươi" is the traditional word for that and carries the severity of the rebuke, though it is otherwise avoided as archaic.

decisions.choice: "linh hồn" (L); "mạng sống" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The soul here is the man's life (meaning decision). Literal keeps "linh hồn" to echo 12:19; Balanced and Readable use "mạng sống", the style guide's word for psychē as life.

decisions.choice: "영혼" (L), "목숨" (B, R) for psychē; "그들이 ... 요구한다" (L), no subject (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the same word as 12:19 so the answer to the rich man's words is seen; the meaning decision reads it as his life. Korean can leave the subject unsaid, as the Greek's indefinite "they" does.

decisions.choice: God speaks to the man in 해라체 ("어리석은 사람아", "-느냐")
decisions.reason: God speaking uses 해라체, as in the Korean style guide (section 7a).

source.text: οὕτως ὁ θησαυρίζων ἑαυτῷ καὶ μὴ εἰς θεὸν πλουτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: So [is] the [one] treasuring up for himself and not toward God being rich.

en.L: So [it is with] the one who stores up treasure for {{gender:themselves|himself}} and is not rich toward God."
en.B: That is how it is for anyone who piles up wealth for {{gender:themselves|himself}} but is not rich in God's sight."
en.R: This is what happens to people who gather riches for themselves but are not rich in the things that matter to God."

es.L: Así [es] el que acumula tesoros para sí y no es rico para con Dios».
es.B: Así le pasa a todo el que amontona riquezas para sí y no es rico a los ojos de Dios».
es.R: Esto es lo que les pasa a los que juntan riquezas para sí mismos, pero no son ricos en lo que a Dios le importa».

fr.L: Ainsi [en est-il de] celui qui amasse des trésors pour lui-même et qui n’est pas riche envers Dieu. »
fr.B: Voilà ce qui arrive à quiconque accumule des richesses pour lui-même sans être riche aux yeux de Dieu. »
fr.R: C’est ce qui arrive aux gens qui amassent des richesses pour eux-mêmes, mais qui ne sont pas riches de ce qui compte pour Dieu. »

sw.L: Ndivyo [ilivyo kwa] mtu anayejilimbikizia hazina, wala si tajiri kwa Mungu."
sw.B: Ndivyo ilivyo kwa kila mtu anayejirundikia mali, lakini si tajiri machoni pa Mungu."
sw.R: Hivi ndivyo itakavyokuwa kwa watu wanaojikusanyia mali, lakini hawana utajiri katika mambo yaliyo muhimu kwa Mungu."

vi.L: Người tích trữ của cải cho mình mà không giàu có đối với Đức Chúa Trời thì cũng [như] vậy."
vi.B: Ai tích trữ của cải cho mình mà không giàu có trước mặt Đức Chúa Trời thì cũng sẽ như vậy."
vi.R: Điều đó sẽ xảy ra cho những người thu góp của cải cho mình mà không giàu có về những điều Đức Chúa Trời coi trọng."

ko.L: 자기를 위하여 재물을 쌓아 두고 하나님을 향하여 부요하지 못한 사람은 이와 같다."
ko.B: 자기를 위해 재물을 쌓아 두면서 하나님 앞에서 부유하지 못한 사람은 누구나 이렇게 된다."
ko.R: 자기를 위해서는 재물을 모으면서, 하나님께서 귀하게 여기시는 것에는 가난한 사람들은 이렇게 될 것이다."

decisions.choice: rich toward God: rich in what God values, by using wealth as God wants
decisions.reason: Jesus goes on to explain: sell possessions and give to those in need, and so have treasure in heaven (12:33-34).

decisions.choice: so: this is how it ends for such a person
alternatives: in this way one should act
decisions.reason: The word applies the parable to everyone like the rich man.

decisions.choice: {{gender:themselves|himself}}
decisions.reason: The saying is for everyone; the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: rich in the things that matter to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: The narrator speaks again in 12:22.

decisions.choice: para sí, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English offers "themselves" with "himself" as the traditional form. Spanish "para sí" is already said of anyone, man or woman, so there is nothing for the setting to change.

decisions.choice: "하나님을 향하여 부요하다" (L); "하나님 앞에서 부유하다" (B); "하나님께서 귀하게 여기시는 것에는 가난한" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads it as rich in what God values; Readable says the opposite side, poor in those things, to keep the sentence short.

source.text: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν, μὴ μεριμνᾶτε τῇ ψυχῇ τί φάγητε, μηδὲ τῷ σώματι τί ἐνδύσησθε.

records.literal_gloss: He said then to the disciples of him, Because of this I say to you, not be anxious for the life what you should eat, nor for the body what you should put on.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Because of this I tell you, do not be anxious about [your] life, what you will eat, nor about [your] body, what you will put on.
en.B: Then Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "That is why I tell you: stop worrying about your life and what you will eat, or about your body and what you will put on it.
en.R: Then Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "So I tell you, do not worry about whether you will have food to eat to stay alive. Do not worry about whether you will have clothes to wear.

es.L: Y dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «Por esto {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: no {{plural_you:se inquieten|os inquietéis}} por la vida, qué {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}}, ni por el cuerpo, qué {{plural_you:vestirán|vestiréis}}.
es.B: Luego Jesús dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: {{plural_you:dejen de preocuparse|dejad de preocuparos}} por {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida y por lo que {{plural_you:van|vais}} a comer, o por {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} cuerpo y por lo que {{plural_you:van a ponerse|vais a poneros}}.
es.R: Luego Jesús dijo a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «Por eso {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: no {{plural_you:se preocupen|os preocupéis}} por si {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} comida para seguir vivos. No {{plural_you:se preocupen|os preocupéis}} por si {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} ropa para vestir.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « C’est pourquoi je vous dis : ne soyez pas en souci de [votre] vie, de ce que vous mangerez, ni de [votre] corps, de ce que vous mettrez sur vous.
fr.B: Puis Jésus dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « Voilà pourquoi je vous le dis : cessez de vous inquiéter pour votre vie et de ce que vous allez manger, ou pour votre corps et de ce que vous allez porter.
fr.R: Puis Jésus a dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « Alors je vous le dis : ne vous inquiétez pas de savoir si vous aurez à manger pour rester en vie. Ne vous inquiétez pas de savoir si vous aurez des vêtements à mettre.

sw.L: Akawaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Kwa sababu hiyo nawaambia, msiwe na wasiwasi juu ya uhai, mtakula nini, wala juu ya mwili, mtavaa nini.
sw.B: Kisha Yesu akawaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Ndiyo sababu nawaambia: acheni kuwa na wasiwasi juu ya uhai wenu na mtakachokula, wala juu ya miili yenu na mtakachovaa.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akawaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Kwa hiyo nawaambia, msiwe na wasiwasi kama mtapata chakula cha kuwaweka hai. Msiwe na wasiwasi kama mtapata nguo za kuvaa.

vi.L: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Vì thế {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, đừng lo lắng về mạng sống, [về việc] các con sẽ ăn gì, cũng đừng lo về thân thể, [về việc] các con sẽ mặc gì.
vi.B: Rồi Đức Giê-xu nói với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Vì thế, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bảo các con, đừng lo lắng cho mạng sống mình, không biết sẽ ăn gì, hay cho thân thể mình, không biết sẽ mặc gì.
vi.R: Rồi Đức Giê-xu nói với các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Vì vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bảo các con, đừng lo lắng không biết có đủ thức ăn để sống không. Đừng lo lắng không biết có đủ quần áo để mặc không.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 그분의 제자들에게 말씀하셨다. "그러므로 내가 너희에게 말한다. 무엇을 먹을지 목숨을 [위하여], 무엇을 입을지 몸을 [위하여] 염려하지 마라.
ko.B: 예수께서 제자들에게 말씀하셨다. "그러므로 내가 너희에게 말한다. 무엇을 먹을까 하고 목숨을 걱정하거나, 무엇을 입을까 하고 몸을 걱정하지 마라.
ko.R: 예수께서 제자들에게 말씀하셨다. "그러니 내가 너희에게 말한다. 살아가는 데 필요한 먹을 것을 걱정하지 마라. 입을 옷도 걱정하지 마라.

decisions.choice: because of this: because life does not come from possessions (12:15-21)
decisions.reason: Jesus draws the lesson of the parable for his disciples. The rich man trusted in what he stored; the disciples, who have little, are not to fret over what they lack.

decisions.choice: be anxious: worry, be troubled in mind
decisions.reason: The verb is about anxiety, not about planning or work. The form tells them to stop worrying or not to start.

decisions.choice: life: life itself, kept going by food
decisions.reason: The word is the one translated "soul" in 12:19-20. Here it is the life that food sustains, set beside the body that clothes cover.

decisions.choice: worry (B, R); be anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled in mind. Literal keeps "be anxious"; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word, as Matthew 6:25 does.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs on to 12:40
decisions.reason: Jesus' words to the disciples in 12:22-40 are one speech.

decisions.choice: uhai
decisions.reason: Here the word is life kept going by food (meaning decision m3). "Uhai" is being alive, as in Matthew 6:25; "uzima" is kept for life itself, as in 12:15.

decisions.choice: "mạng sống" for life (psychē)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 6:25, the parallel saying: life kept going by food (meaning decision) is "mạng sống"; the wording of 12:22-31 follows Matthew 6:25-33 where the Greek is alike.

decisions.choice: "목숨" for psychē, through 12:23; the wording of the Korean Matthew 6:25
decisions.reason: The sayings in 12:22-31 read as the Korean Matthew 6:25-33 does, where the Greek is alike.

source.text: ἡ γὰρ ψυχὴ πλεῖόν ἐστιν τῆς τροφῆς καὶ τὸ σῶμα τοῦ ἐνδύματος.

records.literal_gloss: The for life more is than the food and the body than the clothing.

en.L: For life is more than food, and the body [more] than clothing.
en.B: Life is worth more than food, and the body is worth more than clothing.
en.R: Your life is more important than food. Your body is more important than clothes.

es.L: Porque la vida es más que el alimento, y el cuerpo [más] que el vestido.
es.B: La vida vale más que la comida, y el cuerpo vale más que la ropa.
es.R: {{plural_you:Su|Vuestra}} vida es más importante que la comida. {{plural_you:Su|Vuestro}} cuerpo es más importante que la ropa.

fr.L: Car la vie est plus que la nourriture, et le corps [plus] que le vêtement.
fr.B: La vie vaut plus que la nourriture, et le corps vaut plus que les vêtements.
fr.R: Votre vie est plus importante que la nourriture. Votre corps est plus important que les vêtements.

sw.L: Kwa maana uhai ni zaidi ya chakula, na mwili [zaidi] ya mavazi.
sw.B: Uhai una thamani kuliko chakula, na mwili una thamani kuliko mavazi.
sw.R: Uhai wenu ni muhimu kuliko chakula. Miili yenu ni muhimu kuliko nguo.

vi.L: Vì mạng sống quý hơn thức ăn, và thân thể [quý] hơn quần áo.
vi.B: Mạng sống quý hơn thức ăn, và thân thể quý hơn quần áo.
vi.R: Mạng sống của các con quan trọng hơn thức ăn. Thân thể các con quan trọng hơn quần áo.

ko.L: 목숨이 음식보다 더 [중요하고], 몸이 옷보다 더 [중요하기] 때문이다.
ko.B: 목숨은 음식보다 귀하고, 몸은 옷보다 귀하다.
ko.R: 너희 목숨은 음식보다 더 소중하다. 너희 몸은 옷보다 더 소중하다.

decisions.choice: life is more than food: God who gave the greater gift will give the lesser
alternatives: food and clothing do not matter
decisions.reason: God gave life and the body; he can be trusted for what keeps them going. Food and clothing are needed (12:30), but they are not what life is for.

source.text: κατανοήσατε τοὺς κόρακας ὅτι οὐ σπείρουσιν οὐδὲ θερίζουσιν, οἷς οὐκ ἔστιν ταμεῖον οὐδὲ ἀποθήκη, καὶ ὁ θεὸς τρέφει αὐτούς· πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμεῖς διαφέρετε τῶν πετεινῶν.

records.literal_gloss: Consider the ravens, that not they sow nor reap, to which not is storeroom nor barn, and the God feeds them; how much more you are valuable than the birds!

en.L: Consider the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, they have no storeroom or barn, and God feeds them. How much more valuable you are than the birds!
en.B: Think about the ravens. They do not plant or harvest. They have no storehouse and no barn. Yet God feeds them. And you are worth far more than birds!
en.R: Look at the ravens. They do not plant seeds or gather crops. They do not have buildings to keep food in. But God feeds them. And you are worth much more than birds!

es.L: {{plural_you:Consideren|Considerad}} los cuervos: no siembran ni cosechan, no tienen despensa ni granero, y Dios los alimenta. ¡Cuánto más valiosos {{plural_you:son ustedes|sois vosotros}} que las aves!
es.B: {{plural_you:Piensen|Pensad}} en los cuervos. No siembran ni cosechan. No tienen despensa ni granero. Y aun así Dios los alimenta. ¡Y {{plural_you:ustedes valen|vosotros valéis}} mucho más que las aves!
es.R: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} los cuervos. No plantan semillas ni recogen cosechas. No tienen lugares donde guardar comida. Pero Dios les da de comer. ¡Y {{plural_you:ustedes valen|vosotros valéis}} mucho más que los pájaros!

fr.L: Considérez les corbeaux : ils ne sèment ni ne moissonnent, ils n’ont ni réserve ni grenier, et Dieu les nourrit. Combien plus que les oiseaux vous valez !
fr.B: Pensez aux corbeaux. Ils ne plantent pas et ne récoltent pas. Ils n’ont ni réserve ni grange. Pourtant Dieu les nourrit. Et vous, vous valez bien plus que les oiseaux !
fr.R: Regardez les corbeaux. Ils ne sèment pas de graines et ne font pas de récoltes. Ils n’ont pas de bâtiments pour garder leur nourriture. Mais Dieu les nourrit. Et vous, vous valez beaucoup plus que des oiseaux !

sw.L: Watafakarini kunguru: hawapandi wala hawavuni, hawana chumba cha akiba wala ghala, na Mungu huwalisha. Ninyi mna thamani kubwa kuliko ndege kiasi gani!
sw.B: Fikirieni kunguru. Hawapandi wala hawavuni. Hawana chumba cha akiba wala ghala. Hata hivyo Mungu huwalisha. Nanyi mna thamani kubwa mno kuliko ndege!
sw.R: Waangalieni kunguru. Hawapandi mbegu wala hawavuni mazao. Hawana majengo ya kuwekea chakula. Lakini Mungu huwalisha. Nanyi mna thamani kubwa zaidi kuliko ndege!

vi.L: Hãy suy xét những con quạ: chúng không gieo, không gặt, không có kho chứa hay vựa lúa, thế mà Đức Chúa Trời vẫn nuôi chúng. Các con quý hơn loài chim biết bao!
vi.B: Hãy nghĩ đến những con quạ. Chúng không gieo trồng, cũng không gặt hái. Chúng không có kho chứa, cũng không có vựa lúa. Thế mà Đức Chúa Trời vẫn nuôi chúng. Còn các con lại quý hơn loài chim biết bao!
vi.R: Hãy nhìn những con quạ. Chúng không gieo hạt, không gặt lúa. Chúng không có nhà kho để cất thức ăn. Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời vẫn nuôi chúng. Các con còn quý hơn loài chim nhiều!

ko.L: 까마귀들을 살펴보아라. 그것들은 씨를 뿌리지도 않고 거두지도 않으며, 창고도 곳간도 없다. 그런데도 하나님께서 그것들을 먹이신다. 너희는 새들보다 얼마나 더 귀하냐!
ko.B: 까마귀들을 생각해 보아라. 까마귀는 씨를 뿌리지도, 추수하지도 않는다. 창고도 곳간도 없다. 그래도 하나님께서 까마귀를 먹여 주신다. 너희는 새들보다 훨씬 더 소중하다!
ko.R: 까마귀들을 보아라. 까마귀는 씨를 심지도 않고 곡식을 거두지도 않는다. 먹을 것을 넣어 둘 창고도 없다. 그래도 하나님께서 까마귀를 먹여 주신다. 너희는 새들보다 훨씬 더 소중하다!

decisions.choice: ravens: large black birds that eat what they find, unclean under the law
decisions.reason: Ravens were among the birds Israel was not to eat (Leviticus 11:15). Even these birds, which no one values, God feeds.

decisions.choice: God feeds them: Psalm 147:9 and Job 38:41
decisions.reason: The psalm says that God gives food to the young ravens when they cry; Job asks who provides the raven's food.

decisions.choice: storeroom: an inner room for storing supplies
decisions.reason: It is the same word as "inner rooms" in 12:3. The rich man had barns (12:18); the ravens have nothing at all.

decisions.choice: how much more: from the lesser to the greater
decisions.reason: If God feeds birds, he will surely care for his children (12:7).

decisions.choice: buildings to keep food in
decisions.reason: Readable puts the two words into one plain phrase.

source.text: τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν μεριμνῶν δύναται ἐπὶ τὴν ἡλικίαν αὐτοῦ προσθεῖναι πῆχυν;

records.literal_gloss: Which now of you being anxious is able to the lifespan of him to add a cubit?

en.L: And which of you by being anxious can add a cubit to {{gender:their|his}} span of life?
en.B: Which of you can make your life one hour longer by worrying?
en.R: You cannot make your life even one hour longer by worrying about it.

es.L: ¿Y quién de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, por inquietarse, puede añadir un codo a la duración de su vida?
es.B: ¿Quién de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} puede alargar su vida una sola hora a fuerza de preocuparse?
es.R: Por mucho que {{plural_you:se preocupen|os preocupéis}}, no {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} alargar {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} vida ni una hora.

fr.L: Et qui d’entre vous, en étant en souci, peut ajouter une coudée à la durée de sa vie ?
fr.B: Qui d’entre vous peut, à force de s’inquiéter, allonger sa vie d’une seule heure ?
fr.R: Vous ne pouvez pas allonger votre vie, même d’une heure, en vous inquiétant.

sw.L: Na ni nani kati yenu ambaye, kwa kuwa na wasiwasi, anaweza kuongeza dhiraa moja kwa muda wa maisha yake?
sw.B: Ni nani kati yenu anayeweza kuyaongeza maisha yake hata saa moja kwa kuwa na wasiwasi?
sw.R: Hamwezi kuongeza maisha yenu hata saa moja kwa kuwa na wasiwasi.

vi.L: Và ai trong các con, nhờ lo lắng, có thể thêm vào đời mình một cu-đê?
vi.B: Có ai trong các con nhờ lo lắng mà kéo dài đời mình thêm được một giờ không?
vi.R: Các con không thể sống thêm dù chỉ một giờ nhờ lo lắng.

ko.L: 너희 가운데 누가 염려한다고 해서 자기 수명에 한 규빗이라도 더할 수 있느냐?
ko.B: 너희 가운데 누가 걱정한다고 해서 자기 목숨을 한 시간이라도 늘릴 수 있느냐?
ko.R: 걱정한다고 해서 너희 목숨이 한 시간이라도 늘어나지는 않는다.

decisions.choice: add a cubit to the span of life: lengthen life even a little
alternatives: add a cubit to one's height
decisions.reason: The word can mean length of life or height, and a cubit is about eighteen inches. Adding a cubit to one's height would be no small thing, so the likelier sense is a little more life, as in Matthew 6:27: worry cannot add even a moment.

decisions.choice: one hour
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable turn the picture of a measure into one of time, as the meaning decision explains, and as Matthew 6:27 does. Literal keeps "cubit".

decisions.choice: worrying (B, R); being anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled in mind. Literal keeps "be anxious"; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word, as Matthew 6:25 does.

decisions.choice: {{gender:their|his}}
decisions.reason: The question is for anyone; the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one"; Readable gives it.

decisions.choice: "một cu-đê" (L); "một giờ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 6:27: the cubit measures a span of life, not a distance (meaning decision, with a footnote), so it is not a units setting. Literal keeps the measure in the Protestant form.

decisions.choice: "한 규빗" (L) with no units span; "한 시간" (B, R); "자기" with no gender span
alternatives: a units span on the cubit
decisions.reason: As in the Korean Matthew 6:27: the cubit is a picture of a little more life, not a measure to convert.

source.text: εἰ οὖν οὐδὲ ἐλάχιστον δύνασθε, τί περὶ τῶν λοιπῶν μεριμνᾶτε;

records.literal_gloss: If then not even [the] least you are able, why about the rest are you anxious?

en.L: If then you are not able [to do] even the least thing, why are you anxious about the rest?
en.B: If you cannot manage even something so small, why worry about all the rest?
en.R: You cannot do even a little thing like that. So why should you worry about the other things you need?

es.L: Si, pues, ni siquiera lo más pequeño {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}}, ¿por qué {{plural_you:se inquietan|os inquietáis}} por lo demás?
es.B: Si no {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} ni siquiera algo tan pequeño, ¿por qué {{plural_you:se preocupan|os preocupáis}} por todo lo demás?
es.R: Ni siquiera {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} hacer una cosa tan pequeña como esa. Entonces, ¿por qué {{plural_you:se preocupan|os preocupáis}} por las otras cosas que {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}}?

fr.L: Si donc vous ne pouvez [faire] même la moindre chose, pourquoi êtes-vous en souci du reste ?
fr.B: Si vous ne pouvez rien, même pour une chose aussi petite, pourquoi vous inquiéter de tout le reste ?
fr.R: Vous ne pouvez même pas faire une si petite chose. Alors pourquoi vous inquiéter des autres choses dont vous avez besoin ?

sw.L: Basi ikiwa hamwezi hata jambo dogo kabisa, kwa nini mna wasiwasi juu ya mengine?
sw.B: Ikiwa hamwezi hata jambo dogo hivyo, kwa nini mna wasiwasi juu ya mengine yote?
sw.R: Hamwezi kufanya hata jambo dogo kama hilo. Basi kwa nini mna wasiwasi juu ya mambo mengine mnayohitaji?

vi.L: Vậy nếu ngay cả việc nhỏ nhất các con cũng không làm được, sao các con lại lo lắng về những điều khác?
vi.B: Nếu việc nhỏ như thế các con còn không làm được, sao lại lo lắng về những điều khác?
vi.R: Một việc nhỏ như thế các con còn không làm được. Vậy sao các con lại lo lắng về những thứ khác mình cần?

ko.L: 그러므로 너희가 가장 작은 것도 할 수 없으면서, 왜 나머지 것들에 대하여 염려하느냐?
ko.B: 이렇게 작은 일도 할 수 없으면서, 왜 다른 일들을 걱정하느냐?
ko.R: 너희는 그런 작은 일도 할 수 없다. 그런데 왜 너희에게 필요한 다른 것들을 걱정하느냐?

decisions.choice: if then: since; the condition is true
decisions.reason: The form assumes that the condition holds: they cannot add even that little.

decisions.choice: the rest: food, clothing and the other needs of life
decisions.reason: Adding to one's life is the least thing; providing all the rest is God's work (12:30).

decisions.choice: worry (B, R); be anxious (L)
decisions.reason: The verb means to be anxious or troubled in mind. Literal keeps "be anxious"; Balanced and Readable use the everyday word, as Matthew 6:25 does.

decisions.choice: the other things you need
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the rest" is, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: κατανοήσατε τὰ κρίνα πῶς αὐξάνει· οὐ κοπιᾷ οὐδὲ νήθει· λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν, οὐδὲ Σολομὼν ἐν πάσῃ τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ περιεβάλετο ὡς ἓν τούτων.

records.literal_gloss: Consider the lilies, how they grow: not they toil nor they spin; I say however to you, not even Solomon in all the glory of him was clothed as one of these.

en.L: Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin. But I tell you, not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
en.B: Look at how the lilies grow. They do not work hard or spin thread. But I tell you, Solomon himself, in all his glory, never wore anything as fine as one of them.
en.R: Look at how the wild flowers grow. They do not work or make clothes for themselves. But I tell you, even King Solomon, with all his glory, was never dressed as beautifully as one of these flowers.

es.L: {{plural_you:Consideren|Considerad}} los lirios, cómo crecen: no se fatigan ni hilan; pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que ni siquiera Salomón, en toda su gloria, se vistió como uno de ellos.
es.B: {{plural_you:Fíjense|Fijaos}} en cómo crecen los lirios. No trabajan duro ni hilan. Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que ni el mismo Salomón, con toda su gloria, se vistió nunca con algo tan hermoso como uno de ellos.
es.R: {{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}} cómo crecen las flores silvestres. No trabajan ni se hacen ropa. Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que ni siquiera el rey Salomón, con todas sus riquezas, se vistió nunca tan bonito como una de estas flores.

fr.L: Considérez les lis, comment ils croissent : ils ne peinent ni ne filent. Mais je vous dis : pas même Salomon, dans toute sa gloire, ne s’est vêtu comme l’un d’eux.
fr.B: Regardez comment poussent les lis. Ils ne se fatiguent pas au travail et ne filent pas. Pourtant, je vous le dis, Salomon lui-même, avec toute sa gloire, n’a jamais porté de vêtement aussi beau que l’un d’eux.
fr.R: Regardez comment poussent les fleurs des champs. Elles ne travaillent pas et ne fabriquent pas de vêtements. Pourtant, je vous le dis, même le roi Salomon, avec toute sa gloire, n’a jamais été aussi bien habillé qu’une seule de ces fleurs.

sw.L: Yatafakarini maua jinsi yanavyokua: hayajitaabishi wala hayasokoti nyuzi. Lakini nawaambia, hata Sulemani katika utukufu wake wote hakupambwa kama ua mojawapo kati ya haya.
sw.B: Angalieni jinsi maua ya porini yanavyokua. Hayafanyi kazi ngumu wala hayasokoti nyuzi. Lakini nawaambia, hata Sulemani mwenyewe, pamoja na utukufu wake wote, hakuwahi kuvaa vazi zuri kama ua moja kati ya hayo.
sw.R: Angalieni jinsi maua ya porini yanavyokua. Hayafanyi kazi wala hayajishonei nguo. Lakini nawaambia, hata Mfalme Sulemani, pamoja na utajiri wake wote, hakuwahi kuvaa nguo nzuri kama ua moja kati ya hayo.

vi.L: Hãy suy xét những hoa huệ mọc lên thể nào: chúng không làm lụng cũng không kéo chỉ; nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, ngay cả Sa-lô-môn, trong tất cả vinh quang của ông, cũng không được mặc đẹp như một trong những hoa này.
vi.B: Hãy nghĩ xem hoa dại mọc lên thế nào. Chúng không làm lụng vất vả, cũng không kéo sợi. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, ngay cả Sa-lô-môn trong tất cả vinh quang của ông cũng chưa từng được mặc đẹp như một đóa hoa ấy.
vi.R: Hãy nhìn những bông hoa dại mọc lên thế nào. Chúng không phải làm việc hay tự may quần áo cho mình. Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, ngay cả vua Sa-lô-môn, với tất cả sự giàu sang và vinh quang của mình, cũng không có quần áo đẹp bằng một bông hoa này.

ko.L: 백합들이 어떻게 자라는지 살펴보아라. 그것들은 수고하지도 않고 실을 잣지도 않는다. 그러나 내가 너희에게 말한다. 솔로몬도 그의 모든 영광 가운데 이것들 중 하나만큼 차려입지 못하였다.
ko.B: 백합꽃이 어떻게 자라는지 생각해 보아라. 백합꽃은 애써 일하지도 않고 실을 잣지도 않는다. 그러나 내가 너희에게 말한다. 솔로몬이 온갖 영광을 누릴 때에도 이 꽃 하나만큼 아름답게 차려입지 못했다.
ko.R: 들꽃들이 어떻게 자라는지 보아라. 들꽃은 일하지도 않고 자기 옷을 짓지도 않는다. 그러나 내가 너희에게 말한다. 솔로몬 왕은 아주 부유하고 영광스러웠지만, 그가 입은 옷도 이 꽃 한 송이만큼 아름답지 못했다.

decisions.choice: lilies: wild flowers of the field
decisions.reason: The word is used for lilies and for bright wild flowers in general. 12:28 calls them the grass of the field.

decisions.choice: how they grow: they neither toil nor spin, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: how they neither spin nor weave
decisions.reason: Most manuscripts have "how they grow; they neither toil nor spin", as in Matthew 6:28. A few, mostly Western, have "how they neither spin nor weave". Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Solomon in all his glory: the richest king of Israel
decisions.reason: Solomon's wealth and splendor were famous (1 Kings 10:4-7, 21-23). God dresses a wild flower better than the greatest king could dress himself.

decisions.choice: glory: splendor, magnificence
decisions.reason: Here the word is the splendor of a king's court and robes.

decisions.choice: wild flowers
decisions.reason: Readable uses the general word, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: King Solomon
decisions.reason: Readable says who Solomon was.

decisions.choice: maua (L); maua ya porini (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means wild flowers of the field (meaning decision m1). Swahili "yungiyungi" is the water lily, which is not what is meant, so every level says "maua" (flowers), as in Matthew 6:28.

decisions.choice: "hoa huệ" (L); "hoa dại" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 6:28: the meaning decision says wild flowers in general are meant. Literal keeps the familiar "hoa huệ"; Balanced and Readable say "hoa dại".

decisions.choice: "백합" (L, B), "들꽃" (R); "영광" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the lilies as wild flowers of the field; Balanced keeps the familiar name, Readable says what they are.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ἐν ἀγρῷ τὸν χόρτον ὄντα σήμερον καὶ αὔριον εἰς κλίβανον βαλλόμενον ὁ θεὸς οὕτως ἀμφιέζει, πόσῳ μᾶλλον ὑμᾶς, ὀλιγόπιστοι.

records.literal_gloss: If however in field the grass being today and tomorrow into an oven being thrown the God thus clothes, how much more you, O little-faiths!

en.L: But if God so clothes the grass in the field, which is [here] today and tomorrow is thrown into an oven, how much more [will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} clothe] you, you of little faith!
en.B: If God dresses the wild grass this way, grass that is in the field today and fuel for the oven tomorrow, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will do far more for you. How little faith you have!
en.R: God makes the grass in the fields beautiful like that. But the grass lives only a short time. It is there today, and tomorrow it is burned in an oven. So God will surely give you clothes to wear. You have so little faith!

es.L: Pero si a la hierba que hoy está en el campo y mañana es echada al horno Dios la viste así, ¡cuánto más a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} [{{plural_you:los|os}} vestirá], gente de poca fe!
es.B: Si Dios viste así a la hierba silvestre, que hoy está en el campo y mañana sirve de leña para el horno, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} hará mucho más por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. ¡Qué poca fe {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}}!
es.R: Dios hace que la hierba de los campos sea hermosa así. Pero la hierba vive poco tiempo. Hoy está ahí, y mañana la queman en un horno. Así que Dios, sin duda, {{plural_you:les|os}} dará ropa. ¡{{plural_you:Tienen|Tenéis}} tan poca fe!

fr.L: Mais si Dieu habille ainsi, dans le champ, l’herbe qui est [là] aujourd’hui et qui demain est jetée au four, combien plus vous [habillera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}], gens de peu de foi !
fr.B: Si Dieu habille ainsi l’herbe des champs, qui est là aujourd’hui et qui demain servira à chauffer le four, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fera bien plus pour vous. Que votre foi est petite !
fr.R: Dieu rend l’herbe des champs belle comme cela. Pourtant, l’herbe ne vit pas longtemps. Elle est là aujourd’hui, et demain on la brûle dans un four. Alors Dieu va sûrement vous donner des vêtements à porter. Vous avez si peu de foi !

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa Mungu anayavika hivyo majani yaliyo shambani leo na kesho yanatupwa tanuruni, [atawavika] ninyi zaidi sana kiasi gani, enyi wenye imani ndogo!
sw.B: Ikiwa Mungu huyavika hivyo majani ya porini, yaliyopo shambani leo na kesho ni kuni za tanuru, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atawafanyia ninyi zaidi sana. Imani yenu ni ndogo kweli!
sw.R: Mungu huyafanya majani ya mashambani kuwa mazuri hivyo. Lakini majani huishi muda mfupi tu. Leo yapo, na kesho yanachomwa tanuruni. Kwa hiyo hakika Mungu atawapa nguo za kuvaa. Mna imani ndogo sana!

vi.L: Nhưng nếu Đức Chúa Trời mặc cho cỏ ngoài đồng như vậy, [là thứ] hôm nay còn đó và ngày mai bị ném vào lò, thì [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ mặc cho] các con nhiều hơn biết bao, hỡi những người ít đức tin!
vi.B: Nếu Đức Chúa Trời mặc cho cỏ ngoài đồng như thế, là thứ hôm nay còn đó mà ngày mai đã bị ném vào lò, thì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lại càng mặc cho các con nhiều hơn biết bao, hỡi những người ít đức tin!
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời mặc cho cỏ ngoài đồng đẹp như vậy. Nhưng cỏ chỉ sống một thời gian ngắn. Hôm nay còn đó, ngày mai đã bị đốt trong lò. Vậy chắc chắn Đức Chúa Trời sẽ cho các con quần áo để mặc. Đức tin của các con thật nhỏ bé!

ko.L: 하나님께서 오늘은 들에 있다가 내일은 화덕에 던져지는 풀을 이렇게 입히신다면, 너희는 얼마나 더 [입히시겠느냐]! 믿음이 작은 사람들아.
ko.B: 하나님께서 오늘은 들에 있다가 내일이면 화덕에 던져질 풀도 이렇게 입히시는데, 너희는 얼마나 더 잘 입히시겠느냐! 믿음이 작은 사람들아!
ko.R: 하나님께서는 들풀도 이렇게 아름답게 입혀 주신다. 그 풀은 오늘은 들에 있지만, 내일이면 화덕에 들어가 땔감이 된다. 그러니 하나님께서 너희에게는 틀림없이 입을 것을 주실 것이다. 너희는 믿음이 너무 작구나!

decisions.choice: thrown into an oven: dried grass was used as fuel
decisions.reason: Wood was scarce, and dried grass and weeds fired the clay ovens used for baking.

decisions.choice: you of little faith: people who trust God too little
decisions.reason: The word is a rebuke to disciples whose trust gives way, not a judgment that they have none (Matthew 8:26; 14:31).

decisions.choice: how much more you: the verb "clothe" is understood
alternatives: how much more are you worth
decisions.reason: The sentence leaves out the verb, which carries over from the first half.

decisions.choice: [will he clothe]
decisions.reason: Literal supplies the verb in brackets, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: statements instead of a condition
decisions.reason: Readable sets out the argument in short steps.

decisions.choice: [{{plural_you:los|os}} vestirá], with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English Literal supplies "[will he clothe]" with the setting on "he". Spanish leaves the subject in the verb ending, where there is nothing to capitalise; Balanced says "él" and carries the span, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: "những người ít đức tin" (L, B); "Đức tin của các con thật nhỏ bé" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 6:30 and Mark 4:40: one Greek word, "little-faiths", said with the key term "đức tin" at every level. Balanced keeps the address, as in Matthew, where the English Balanced makes it an exclamation.

decisions.choice: "믿음이 작은 사람들아" (L, B), "너희는 믿음이 너무 작구나!" (R); "화덕" for the oven
decisions.reason: As settled for the Korean Matthew 6:30.

source.text: καὶ ὑμεῖς μὴ ζητεῖτε τί φάγητε καὶ τί πίητε, καὶ μὴ μετεωρίζεσθε, ταῦτα γὰρ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη τοῦ κόσμου ἐπιζητοῦσιν, ὑμῶν δὲ ὁ πατὴρ οἶδεν ὅτι χρῄζετε τούτων.

records.literal_gloss: And you not seek what you might eat and what you might drink, and not be in suspense; \v 30 these things for all the nations of the world seek after, of you now the Father knows that you have need of these.

en.L: And you, do not seek what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be unsettled; \v 30 for all the nations of the world seek after these things, but your Father knows that you need them.
en.B: So do not be always looking for what you will eat and what you will drink, and do not be on edge about it. \v 30 These are the things that the nations of the world chase after, but your Father knows that you need them.
en.R: So do not spend your time thinking about what you will eat and drink. Do not be upset about it. \v 30 People all over the world who do not know God are always running after these things. But your Father knows that you need them.

es.L: Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, no {{plural_you:busquen|busquéis}} qué {{plural_you:comerán|comeréis}} y qué {{plural_you:beberán|beberéis}}, ni {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} en vilo; \v 30 porque todas estas cosas las buscan con afán las naciones del mundo, pero {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre sabe que {{plural_you:las necesitan|las necesitáis}}.
es.B: Así que no {{plural_you:anden|andéis}} siempre buscando qué comer y qué beber, ni {{plural_you:vivan|viváis}} con el alma en vilo por eso. \v 30 Esas son las cosas que persiguen las naciones del mundo, pero {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre sabe que {{plural_you:las necesitan|las necesitáis}}.
es.R: Así que no {{plural_you:pasen|paséis}} el tiempo pensando en qué {{plural_you:van|vais}} a comer y a beber. No {{plural_you:se angustien|os angustiéis}} por eso. \v 30 La gente de todo el mundo que no conoce a Dios siempre anda detrás de esas cosas. Pero {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre sabe que {{plural_you:las necesitan|las necesitáis}}.

fr.L: Et vous, ne cherchez pas ce que vous mangerez et ce que vous boirez, et ne vous laissez pas agiter ; \v 30 car toutes ces choses, les nations du monde les recherchent, mais votre Père sait que vous en avez besoin.
fr.B: Ne passez donc pas votre temps à chercher ce que vous allez manger et boire, et ne vous mettez pas dans tous vos états pour cela. \v 30 Ce sont les nations du monde qui courent après tout cela, mais votre Père sait que vous en avez besoin.
fr.R: Alors ne passez pas votre temps à penser à ce que vous allez manger et boire. Ne soyez pas troublés à ce sujet. \v 30 Partout dans le monde, les gens qui ne connaissent pas Dieu courent toujours après ces choses. Mais votre Père sait que vous en avez besoin.

sw.L: Nanyi msitafute mtakula nini na mtakunywa nini, wala msiwe na mioyo inayoyumbayumba; \v 30 kwa maana mataifa yote ya ulimwengu huyatafuta hayo yote, lakini Baba yenu anajua kwamba mnayahitaji.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo msiwe kila mara mkitafuta mtakula nini na mtakunywa nini, wala msihangaike juu ya hayo. \v 30 Hayo ndiyo mambo ambayo watu wa mataifa ya ulimwengu huyakimbilia, lakini Baba yenu anajua kwamba mnayahitaji.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo msitumie muda wenu kufikiri mtakula nini na mtakunywa nini. Msifadhaike juu ya hayo. \v 30 Watu wasiomjua Mungu duniani kote daima wanayakimbilia mambo hayo. Lakini Baba yenu anajua kwamba mnayahitaji.

vi.L: Còn các con, đừng tìm kiếm mình sẽ ăn gì, uống gì, và đừng băn khoăn; \v 30 vì tất cả các dân tộc trên thế gian đều tìm kiếm những điều này, nhưng Cha các con biết các con cần những điều ấy.
vi.B: Vậy các con đừng cứ mải tìm xem mình sẽ ăn gì, uống gì, và đừng bồn chồn lo âu. \v 30 Vì đó là những điều mà các dân ngoại đạo trên thế gian vẫn chạy theo, còn Cha các con biết các con cần những thứ ấy.
vi.R: Vậy đừng mất thì giờ nghĩ xem mình sẽ ăn gì, uống gì. Đừng lo âu về những điều ấy. \v 30 Những người khắp thế gian không biết Đức Chúa Trời lúc nào cũng chạy theo những thứ ấy. Nhưng Cha các con biết các con cần những thứ đó.

ko.L: 그리고 너희는 무엇을 먹을지, 무엇을 마실지 찾지 말고, 마음을 졸이지도 마라. \v 30 이 모든 것은 세상의 이방인들이 찾아 구하는 것이기 때문이다. 그러나 너희 아버지께서는 너희에게 이것들이 필요하다는 것을 아신다.
ko.B: 그러니 무엇을 먹을까, 무엇을 마실까 늘 찾아다니지 말고, 그 일로 마음을 졸이지도 마라. \v 30 이런 것들은 모두 세상의 이방 사람들이 애써 구하는 것이다. 너희 아버지께서는 너희에게 이것들이 필요하다는 것을 알고 계신다.
ko.R: 그러니 무엇을 먹고 무엇을 마실지 그런 생각만 하며 지내지 마라. 그 일로 불안해하지도 마라. \v 30 세상에서 하나님을 모르는 사람들은 늘 이런 것들을 얻으려고 애쓴다. 그러나 너희 아버지께서는 너희에게 이런 것들이 필요하다는 것을 아신다.

decisions.choice: be unsettled: be anxious, tossed between hope and fear
decisions.reason: The verb first meant to be raised up in the air, and so to be unsteady or in suspense. In Greek outside the Bible it can also mean to be proud, but here, beside "seek" and "be anxious", it means to be restless with worry.

decisions.choice: the nations of the world: the peoples who do not know God
decisions.reason: "The nations" means the Gentiles, the peoples outside Israel who did not worship the God of Israel. Here the point is people who live without trusting God as Father. The world here is humankind.

decisions.choice: your Father knows: God cares for his children as a father
decisions.reason: Jesus calls God the disciples' Father (6:36; 11:2, 13). A father who knows what his children need will give it.

decisions.choice: be on edge about it (B); be upset about it (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use everyday words for a restless, anxious state, different from the verb rendered "worry" in 12:22.

decisions.choice: People all over the world who do not know God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the nations", as the meaning decision does.

decisions.choice: estar en vilo (L); vivir con el alma en vilo (B); angustiarse (R)
decisions.reason: This verb is not the one for "be anxious" in 12:22-26 but a picture of being tossed between hope and fear (meaning decision m1). "En vilo" is that suspense; "inquietarse" is kept for the other verb.

decisions.choice: las naciones del mundo (L, B); la gente de todo el mundo que no conoce a Dios (R)
decisions.reason: The peoples who do not know God (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep "naciones", the book-wide word with "the world"; Readable says what is meant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: msiwe na mioyo inayoyumbayumba (L); msihangaike (B); msifadhaike (R)
decisions.reason: This verb is not the one for "be anxious" in 12:22-26 but a picture of being tossed between hope and fear (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the picture of a swaying heart; "kuwa na wasiwasi" is kept for the other verb.

decisions.choice: mataifa ya ulimwengu (L); watu wa mataifa ya ulimwengu (B); watu wasiomjua Mungu duniani kote (R)
decisions.reason: The peoples who do not know God (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep "mataifa", the book-wide word, with "ulimwengu"; Readable says what is meant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "các dân tộc trên thế gian" (L); "các dân ngoại đạo trên thế gian" (B); "những người khắp thế gian không biết Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: The nations of the world are the peoples who do not know God (meaning decision). Literal keeps "the nations"; Balanced and Readable say what kind of people they are, as Matthew 6:32 does.

decisions.choice: "이방인들" (L), "이방 사람들" (B), "하나님을 모르는 사람들" (R) for "the nations"
decisions.reason: The words settled for "Gentiles" in the Korean Matthew; the meaning decision reads "the nations of the world" as the peoples who do not know God.

decisions.choice: "마음을 졸이다" (L, B), "불안해하다" (R) for meteōrizomai
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the word as anxious, tossed between hope and fear.

source.text: πλὴν ζητεῖτε τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ταῦτα προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: But seek the kingdom of him, and these things will be added to you.

en.L: Rather, seek {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom, and these things will be added to you.
en.B: Instead, set your hearts on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} kingdom, and you will receive these things besides.
en.R: Instead, make God's kingdom the most important thing you look for. Then God will give you these other things too.

es.L: Más bien, {{plural_you:busquen|buscad}} {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} reino, y estas cosas {{plural_you:se les|se os}} darán por añadidura.
es.B: Al contrario, {{plural_you:pongan|poned}} el corazón en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} reino, y además {{plural_you:recibirán|recibiréis}} estas cosas.
es.R: Al contrario, {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} que el reino de Dios sea lo más importante que {{plural_you:buscan|buscáis}}. Entonces Dios también {{plural_you:les|os}} dará esas otras cosas.

fr.L: Cherchez plutôt {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume, et ces choses vous seront ajoutées.
fr.B: Attachez plutôt votre cœur à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} royaume, et vous recevrez cela en plus.
fr.R: Mettez plutôt le royaume de Dieu à la première place dans ce que vous cherchez. Alors Dieu vous donnera aussi ces autres choses.

sw.L: Bali tafuteni ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, na hayo mtaongezewa.
sw.B: Badala yake, iwekeni mioyo yenu katika ufalme {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, nanyi mtapewa mambo hayo pia.
sw.R: Badala yake, fanyeni ufalme wa Mungu kuwa jambo la kwanza mnalolitafuta. Ndipo Mungu atawapa mambo hayo mengine pia.

vi.L: Nhưng hãy tìm kiếm vương quốc của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, thì những điều này sẽ được thêm cho các con.
vi.B: Thay vào đó, hãy để lòng tìm kiếm vương quốc của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, rồi các con sẽ được ban cho cả những điều ấy nữa.
vi.R: Thay vào đó, hãy tìm kiếm vương quốc của Đức Chúa Trời trên hết mọi sự. Rồi Đức Chúa Trời sẽ ban cho các con cả những thứ kia nữa.

ko.L: 오히려 그분의 나라를 구하여라. 그러면 이것들이 너희에게 더하여질 것이다.
ko.B: 오히려 그분의 나라를 구하여라. 그러면 이것들도 너희에게 주어질 것이다.
ko.R: 그 대신 하나님의 나라를 가장 먼저 구하여라. 그러면 하나님께서 이런 것들도 너희에게 주실 것이다.

decisions.choice: his kingdom, the reading of the SBLGNT
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts have "his kingdom". Many others have "the kingdom of God", which is how Matthew 6:33 begins the phrase. The sense is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: will be added: God will give them as well
decisions.reason: The passive leaves God as the giver (12:30).

decisions.choice: seek his kingdom: make God's rule the aim of life
alternatives: look for a place called the kingdom
decisions.reason: To seek the kingdom is to want God's rule more than anything, to live under it and to pray for it to come (11:2).

decisions.choice: God's kingdom; God will give you
decisions.reason: Readable names God, as the meaning decisions explain.

decisions.choice: "그분의 나라" (L, B), "하나님의 나라" (R)
decisions.reason: "그분" honours the Father of 12:30 without a setting span.

source.text: Μὴ φοβοῦ, τὸ μικρὸν ποίμνιον, ὅτι εὐδόκησεν ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν δοῦναι ὑμῖν τὴν βασιλείαν.

records.literal_gloss: Not fear, the little flock, for took delight the Father of you to give you the kingdom.

en.L: Do not fear, little flock, because your Father has been glad to give you the kingdom.
en.B: Do not be afraid, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} little flock. Your Father has gladly chosen to give you the kingdom.
en.R: My little flock, you do not need to be afraid. Your Father in heaven is happy to give you the kingdom.

es.L: No temas, pequeño rebaño, porque a {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre le ha agradado {{plural_you:darles|daros}} el reino.
es.B: No tengas miedo, pequeño rebaño {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}. {{plural_you:Su|Vuestro}} Padre ha decidido con gusto {{plural_you:darles|daros}} el reino.
es.R: Pequeño rebaño {{deity_pronoun:mío|Mío}}, no tienes por qué tener miedo. {{plural_you:El Padre de ustedes|Vuestro Padre}} que está en el cielo se alegra de {{plural_you:darles|daros}} el reino.

fr.L: Ne crains pas, petit troupeau, car il a plu à votre Père de vous donner le royaume.
fr.B: N’aie pas peur, {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} petit troupeau. Votre Père a choisi avec joie de vous donner le royaume.
fr.R: Mon petit troupeau, tu n’as pas à avoir peur. Votre Père qui est dans le ciel est heureux de vous donner le royaume.

sw.L: Usiogope, ewe kundi dogo, kwa sababu Baba yenu amependezwa kuwapa ufalme.
sw.B: Usiogope, ewe kundi {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} dogo. Baba yenu ameamua kwa furaha kuwapa ufalme.
sw.R: Kundi {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} dogo, huna haja ya kuogopa. Baba yenu aliye mbinguni anafurahi kuwapa ufalme.

vi.L: Đừng sợ, hỡi bầy nhỏ, vì Cha các con đã vui lòng ban vương quốc cho các con.
vi.B: Hỡi bầy nhỏ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, đừng sợ. Cha các con đã vui lòng ban vương quốc cho các con.
vi.R: Hỡi bầy chiên nhỏ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, các con không cần phải sợ. Cha các con ở trên trời vui lòng ban vương quốc cho các con.

ko.L: 두려워하지 마라, 작은 양 떼야. 너희 아버지께서 너희에게 그 나라를 주시기를 기뻐하셨기 때문이다.
ko.B: 내 작은 양 떼야, 두려워하지 마라. 너희 아버지께서 그 나라를 너희에게 기쁘게 주시기로 하셨다.
ko.R: 내 작은 양 떼야, 무서워할 것 없다. 하늘에 계신 너희 아버지께서는 그 나라를 너희에게 주시는 것을 기뻐하신다.

decisions.choice: little flock: God's people pictured as sheep, few and weak
alternatives: a group with no special meaning
decisions.reason: The prophets speak of Israel as the flock of God, whom he shepherds (Isaiah 40:11; Ezekiel 34:11-16). The disciples are few and have no power, but they are God's flock.

decisions.choice: has been glad: has chosen with pleasure, has decided gladly
decisions.reason: The verb is used of God's good will and choice (3:22; Colossians 1:19). The kingdom is the Father's free gift, not a prize to be won.

decisions.choice: to give you the kingdom: Daniel 7:18, 27
decisions.reason: Daniel saw the kingdom given to the holy people of the Most High. Jesus promises it to his small group of followers (22:29).

decisions.choice: my little flock
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "my", since Jesus speaks to his own followers. Literal keeps the plain address.

decisions.choice: Your Father in heaven
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the Father is God (11:13).

decisions.choice: No temas / No tengas miedo (singular, no plural_you span), then {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} Padre, {{plural_you:darles|daros}}
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks to the little flock as one, with a singular verb, and then turns to the plural "your Father ... to give you" (meaning decision m1). Spanish can show both, as English cannot: "tú" for the flock, which has no setting, and the plural forms after it.

decisions.choice: "tu" for the little flock, "vous" for its members ("Ne crains pas … votre Père … vous donner")
decisions.reason: The Greek addresses the flock in the singular and then says "your Father" and "to you" in the plural. French follows the Greek number, as the style guide asks, and the switch reads naturally because "troupeau" is one word for many people.

decisions.choice: Usiogope (singular), then Baba yenu, kuwapa (plural)
decisions.reason: The Greek speaks to the little flock as one, with a singular verb, and then turns to the plural "your Father ... to give you" (meaning decision m1). Swahili can show both, as English cannot: the singular for the flock, the plural after it.

decisions.choice: "bầy nhỏ" (L, B); "bầy chiên nhỏ" (R)
decisions.reason: God's people are pictured as a flock, few and weak (meaning decision); Literal and Balanced keep the Greek's single word, Readable names the sheep.

source.text: πωλήσατε τὰ ὑπάρχοντα ὑμῶν καὶ δότε ἐλεημοσύνην· ποιήσατε ἑαυτοῖς βαλλάντια μὴ παλαιούμενα, θησαυρὸν ἀνέκλειπτον ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς, ὅπου κλέπτης οὐκ ἐγγίζει οὐδὲ σὴς διαφθείρει·

records.literal_gloss: Sell the possessions of you and give alms; make for yourselves purses not growing old, a treasure unfailing in the heavens, where thief not draws near nor moth destroys.

en.L: Sell your possessions and give alms. Make for yourselves purses that do not grow old, an unfailing treasure in the heavens, where no thief comes near and no moth destroys.
en.B: Sell what you own and give the money to people in need. Get yourselves money bags that never wear out, a treasure in heaven that will never run out. No thief can get near it there, and no moth can spoil it.
en.R: Sell the things you own and give the money to poor people. Then you will have a treasure in heaven that will last forever. It will be like a purse that never wears out. No thief can steal it, and no moth can eat it.

es.L: {{plural_you:Vendan|Vended}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} bienes y {{plural_you:den|dad}} limosna. {{plural_you:Háganse|Haceos}} bolsas que no envejecen, un tesoro inagotable en los cielos, adonde el ladrón no se acerca ni la polilla destruye.
es.B: {{plural_you:Vendan|Vended}} lo que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} y {{plural_you:den|dad}} el dinero a los necesitados. {{plural_you:Consíganse|Conseguíos}} bolsas que nunca se gastan, un tesoro en el cielo que nunca se acaba. Allí ningún ladrón puede acercarse, y ninguna polilla puede echarlo a perder.
es.R: {{plural_you:Vendan|Vended}} las cosas que {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} y {{plural_you:den|dad}} el dinero a los pobres. Así {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} en el cielo un tesoro que durará para siempre. Será como una bolsa de dinero que nunca se gasta. Ningún ladrón podrá robarlo, y ninguna polilla podrá comérselo.

fr.L: Vendez vos biens et faites l’aumône. Faites-vous des bourses qui ne vieillissent pas, un trésor inépuisable dans les cieux, où le voleur n’approche pas et où la mite ne détruit pas.
fr.B: Vendez ce que vous possédez et donnez l’argent à ceux qui sont dans le besoin. Procurez-vous des bourses qui ne s’usent jamais, un trésor dans le ciel qui ne s’épuisera jamais. Là, aucun voleur ne peut s’en approcher, et aucune mite ne peut l’abîmer.
fr.R: Vendez ce que vous avez et donnez l’argent aux pauvres. Alors vous aurez un trésor dans le ciel, qui durera toujours. Ce sera comme une bourse qui ne s’use jamais. Aucun voleur ne pourra le voler, et aucune mite ne pourra le manger.

sw.L: Uzeni mali zenu mtoe sadaka. Jifanyieni mifuko isiyochakaa, hazina isiyopungua mbinguni, ambako mwizi hakaribii wala nondo haharibu.
sw.B: Uzeni mlivyo navyo, mkawape wahitaji fedha hizo. Jipatieni mifuko ya fedha isiyochakaa kamwe, hazina mbinguni isiyokwisha. Huko hakuna mwizi anayeweza kuikaribia, wala nondo anayeweza kuiharibu.
sw.R: Uzeni vitu mlivyo navyo, mkawape maskini fedha hizo. Hapo mtakuwa na hazina mbinguni itakayodumu milele. Itakuwa kama mfuko wa fedha usiochakaa kamwe. Hakuna mwizi atakayeweza kuiiba, wala nondo atakayeweza kuila.

vi.L: Hãy bán tài sản của các con mà bố thí. Hãy làm cho mình những túi tiền không hề cũ mòn, một kho của cải không hề cạn trên các tầng trời, nơi kẻ trộm không đến gần, mối mọt không làm hư hại.
vi.B: Hãy bán tài sản mình đi và đem tiền giúp người túng thiếu. Hãy sắm cho mình những túi tiền không bao giờ sờn rách, một kho của cải không bao giờ cạn ở trên trời. Ở đó kẻ trộm không đến gần được, và mối mọt không làm hư hại được.
vi.R: Hãy bán những gì các con có và đem tiền cho người nghèo. Như vậy các con sẽ có của cải ở trên trời, là thứ còn mãi mãi. Của cải ấy giống như một túi tiền không bao giờ rách. Không kẻ trộm nào lấy cắp được, và không con mọt nào cắn phá được.

ko.L: 너희 소유를 팔아 자선을 베풀어라. 너희를 위하여 낡지 않는 돈주머니, 곧 하늘에 있는 다함이 없는 보물을 만들어라. 거기는 도둑이 가까이 오지도 못하고 좀이 망가뜨리지도 못한다.
ko.B: 너희가 가진 것을 팔아서 가난한 사람들에게 주어라. 낡지 않는 돈주머니를 너희를 위해 마련하여라. 그것은 하늘에 쌓아 두는, 결코 없어지지 않는 보물이다. 거기에는 도둑이 다가오지도 못하고 좀이 먹지도 못한다.
ko.R: 너희가 가진 것을 팔아서 그 돈을 가난한 사람들에게 주어라. 그러면 하늘에 영원히 없어지지 않는 보물이 생길 것이다. 그것은 해지지 않는 돈주머니와 같다. 거기에는 도둑이 훔쳐 가지도 못하고 좀이 먹지도 못한다.

decisions.choice: alms: gifts to the poor
decisions.reason: Giving to the poor was a duty of the law (Deuteronomy 15:7-11) and a mark of true devotion (11:41; Acts 10:2).

decisions.choice: treasure in the heavens: what God keeps for those who give
decisions.reason: What is given away for God is kept by God. Jesus says the same to the rich ruler (18:22).

decisions.choice: purses; moth: a money bag wears out, and moths eat stored cloth
decisions.reason: Wealth was often kept as fine clothing, which moths could ruin, and money was carried in a leather bag. Treasure with God is safe from both.

decisions.choice: heavens: heaven, where God is
decisions.reason: The plural follows a Hebrew way of speaking and means heaven.

decisions.choice: give the money to people in need (B); give the money to poor people (R)
decisions.reason: "Alms" is an old word. Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: the treasure first, then the purse as a picture
decisions.reason: Readable puts the plain statement first and the picture after it.

decisions.choice: "tài sản" for possessions; "của cải" for the treasure (12:33-34)
decisions.reason: Matthew 6:19-21 uses "của cải" for the treasure in the parallel saying, so Luke 12:34 reads like Matthew 6:21; "tài sản" keeps the possessions apart.

decisions.choice: "trên các tầng trời" (L); "ở trên trời" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke writes the plural "the heavens" here (meaning decision); Literal keeps it as in Matthew, the other levels use the ordinary phrase.

decisions.choice: "자선을 베풀다" (L), "가난한 사람들에게 주다" (B, R), as in 11:41; "보물" at every level
decisions.reason: Here the treasure is kept in heaven, and "보물" keeps the link with 12:34 at every level.

source.text: ὅπου γάρ ἐστιν ὁ θησαυρὸς ὑμῶν, ἐκεῖ καὶ ἡ καρδία ὑμῶν ἔσται.

records.literal_gloss: Where for is the treasure of you, there also the heart of you will be.

en.L: For where your treasure is, there your heart also will be.
en.B: Your heart will be wherever your treasure is.
en.R: Your heart will always be with the things you treasure most.

es.L: Porque donde está {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} tesoro, allí estará también {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón.
es.B: {{plural_you:Su|Vuestro}} corazón estará dondequiera que esté {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} tesoro.
es.R: {{plural_you:Su|Vuestro}} corazón estará siempre con las cosas que {{plural_you:ustedes más valoran|vosotros más valoráis}}.

fr.L: Car où se trouve votre trésor, là aussi se trouvera votre cœur.
fr.B: Votre cœur sera là où est votre trésor.
fr.R: Votre cœur sera toujours auprès des choses auxquelles vous tenez le plus.

sw.L: Kwa maana pale ilipo hazina yenu, hapo pia moyo wenu utakuwa.
sw.B: Moyo wenu utakuwa pale ilipo hazina yenu.
sw.R: Moyo wenu utakuwa daima pamoja na vitu mnavyovithamini kuliko vyote.

vi.L: Vì của cải các con ở đâu, thì lòng các con cũng sẽ ở đó.
vi.B: Của cải các con ở đâu, thì lòng các con cũng sẽ ở đó.
vi.R: Lòng các con sẽ luôn hướng về những gì các con quý nhất.

ko.L: 너희 보물이 있는 곳, 거기에 너희 마음도 있을 것이기 때문이다.
ko.B: 너희 마음은 너희 보물이 있는 곳에 있게 마련이다.
ko.R: 너희 마음은 언제나 너희가 가장 소중하게 여기는 것에 가 있을 것이다.

decisions.choice: heart: the center of a person, where desire, thought and will are
decisions.reason: In Scripture the heart is the inner self that decides and loves. What a person treasures draws the whole self after it.

decisions.choice: for: the reason for 12:33
decisions.reason: Treasure in heaven matters because the heart goes where the treasure is.

decisions.choice: the heart first
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the main point first, in plain order.

decisions.choice: "lòng" for the heart
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 6:21 and 12:34: the center of desire, thought and will (meaning decision) is "lòng"; "tim" is the organ.

decisions.choice: "너희" for the plural "your"
decisions.reason: Luke's Greek has the plural here, where Matthew's has the singular.

source.text: Ἔστωσαν ὑμῶν αἱ ὀσφύες περιεζωσμέναι καὶ οἱ λύχνοι καιόμενοι, καὶ ὑμεῖς ὅμοιοι ἀνθρώποις προσδεχομένοις τὸν κύριον ἑαυτῶν πότε ἀναλύσῃ ἐκ τῶν γάμων, ἵνα ἐλθόντος καὶ κρούσαντος εὐθέως ἀνοίξωσιν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: Let be of you the waists girded and the lamps burning, \v 36 and you like to men waiting for the master of themselves, when he might return from the wedding feasts, that having come and having knocked immediately they might open to him.

en.L: Let your waists be girded and your lamps burning, \v 36 and be like {{gender:people|men}} waiting for their master, when he returns from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks they may open to him at once.
en.B: Stay ready for work, with your belt tied and your lamp lit. \v 36 Be like {{gender:people|men}} who are waiting for their master to come home from a wedding feast, ready to open the door the moment he arrives and knocks.
en.R: Be ready to work. Tuck your robe into your belt and keep a lamp lit. \v 36 Be like a household of servants waiting up for their master on the night he comes back from a wedding party. They want to be ready to open the door as soon as he knocks.

es.L: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} la cintura ceñida y las lámparas ardiendo, \v 36 y {{plural_you:sean|sed}} semejantes a {{gender:personas|hombres}} que esperan a su señor cuando vuelva de las bodas, para que, cuando llegue y llame, le abran enseguida.
es.B: {{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} listos para el trabajo, con el cinturón bien atado y la lámpara encendida. \v 36 {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} como {{gender:personas|hombres}} que esperan a que su señor vuelva de un banquete de bodas, listos para abrirle la puerta en cuanto llegue y llame.
es.R: {{plural_you:Estén|Estad}} listos para trabajar. {{plural_you:Cíñanse|Ceñíos}} la ropa con el cinturón y {{plural_you:tengan|tened}} una lámpara encendida. \v 36 {{plural_you:Sean|Sed}} como los siervos de una casa que esperan despiertos a su señor la noche en que vuelve de una fiesta de bodas. Quieren estar listos para abrirle la puerta en cuanto llame.

fr.L: Ayez les reins ceints et les lampes allumées, \v 36 et vous, [soyez] semblables à des {{gender:gens|hommes}} qui attendent leur maître, au moment où il reviendra des noces, afin que, dès qu’il arrivera et frappera, ils lui ouvrent aussitôt.
fr.B: Soyez prêts à travailler, la ceinture serrée et la lampe allumée. \v 36 Soyez comme des {{gender:gens|hommes}} qui attendent que leur maître revienne d’un repas de noces, prêts à lui ouvrir la porte dès qu’il arrivera et frappera.
fr.R: Soyez prêts à travailler. Relevez votre tunique dans votre ceinture et gardez une lampe allumée. \v 36 Soyez comme les serviteurs d’une maison qui veillent en attendant leur maître, le soir où il revient d’une fête de mariage. Ils veulent être prêts à lui ouvrir la porte dès qu’il frappera.

sw.L: Mwe mmejifunga mishipi viunoni, na taa zenu zikiwaka; \v 36 nanyi mwe kama watu wanaomngoja bwana wao, atakaporudi kutoka harusini, ili akija na kubisha hodi wamfungulie mara moja.
sw.B: Kaeni tayari kwa kazi, mkiwa mmejifunga mishipi na taa zenu zikiwaka. \v 36 Mwe kama watu wanaomngoja bwana wao arudi nyumbani kutoka karamu ya harusi, wakiwa tayari kumfungulia mlango mara tu atakapofika na kubisha hodi.
sw.R: Kuweni tayari kufanya kazi. Kunjeni kanzu zenu na kuzifunga kwa mishipi, na taa zenu ziwe zinawaka. \v 36 Mwe kama watumishi wa nyumba wanaomsubiri bwana wao usiku anaporudi kutoka sherehe ya harusi. Wanataka kuwa tayari kumfungulia mlango mara tu anapobisha hodi.

vi.L: Hãy thắt lưng các con lại và để đèn các con cháy sáng, \v 36 và hãy giống như những người đang chờ chủ mình khi chủ đi dự tiệc cưới trở về, để khi chủ đến gõ cửa, họ mở cửa cho chủ ngay.
vi.B: Hãy luôn sẵn sàng làm việc, lưng thắt gọn gàng và đèn thắp sáng. \v 36 Hãy giống như những người đang chờ chủ mình đi dự tiệc cưới trở về, sẵn sàng mở cửa ngay khi chủ về đến và gõ cửa.
vi.R: Hãy sẵn sàng để làm việc. Hãy buộc gọn áo vào thắt lưng và giữ cho đèn luôn cháy sáng. \v 36 Hãy giống như những đầy tớ trong nhà thức chờ chủ mình đi dự tiệc cưới về trong đêm. Họ muốn sẵn sàng mở cửa ngay khi chủ gõ cửa.

ko.L: 너희 허리에는 띠를 두르고, 너희 등불은 켜 두어라. \v 36 그리고 너희는 혼인 잔치에서 언제 돌아올지 모르는 자기 주인을 기다리는 사람들과 같이 되어라. 주인이 와서 문을 두드리면 곧 열어 주려는 사람들이다.
ko.B: 일할 차림으로 허리띠를 단단히 매고, 등불을 켜 둔 채 준비하고 있어라. \v 36 혼인 잔치에서 돌아오는 주인을 기다리는 사람들처럼 되어라. 그들은 주인이 와서 문을 두드리면 곧바로 문을 열어 주려고 기다린다.
ko.R: 언제든지 일할 수 있게 준비하고 있어라. 옷자락을 걷어 허리띠에 끼우고, 등불을 켜 두어라. \v 36 주인이 혼인 잔치에서 돌아오는 밤에 자지 않고 기다리는 종들처럼 되어라. 그 종들은 주인이 와서 문을 두드리면 바로 문을 열어 주려고 기다린다.

decisions.choice: let your waists be girded: be dressed and ready for action
decisions.reason: People wore long robes. To work, travel or run, they pulled the robe up and tucked it into a belt (Exodus 12:11; 1 Kings 18:46).

decisions.choice: wedding feast: a celebration that could last late into the night, or for days
decisions.reason: No one could know when a guest would come home from such a feast. The slaves must stay ready all night.

decisions.choice: people: here the slaves of the household (12:37)
decisions.reason: The word means human beings; 12:37 shows they are the master's slaves.

decisions.choice: master: the owner of the household
alternatives: Lord as a title of Jesus
decisions.reason: The word is the one used for "Lord". In the parable it is a slave owner; Peter's question in 12:41 and the saying in 12:40 show that Jesus is speaking of his own return.

decisions.choice: Stay ready for work, with your belt tied (B); Tuck your robe into your belt (R)
decisions.reason: "Gird" is an old word. Balanced and Readable describe what it meant.

decisions.choice: {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The picture is of a whole household of slaves, and the saying is for every disciple; the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: a household of servants
decisions.reason: Readable names the people as the household's servants from the start, as 12:37 calls them. The Greek here says only "men".

decisions.choice: Ayez les reins ceints (L)
decisions.reason: French says "avoir les reins ceints" for being dressed for action, and the word fits the Greek one for the waist; a plural "vos tailles" would sound odd. Balanced and Readable say what it meant, as in English.

decisions.choice: "chủ" for the master (12:36-47)
decisions.reason: The master is the owner of the household (meaning decision), a figure in the parable; "chủ" says it plainly, as "chủ nhà" in Mark 13:35, and the words for him take no setting span.

decisions.choice: "허리에 띠를 두르다" (L); "일할 차림으로 허리띠를 단단히 매다" (B); "옷자락을 걷어 허리띠에 끼우다" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the idiom as being dressed and ready for action; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: "사람들" (L, B) with no gender span, "종들" (R); "곧" (L), "곧바로" (B), "바로" (R) for eutheōs
alternatives: a gender span with "남자들" as the alternative
decisions.reason: "사람들" already includes men and women; eutheōs is rendered as euthys is in the Korean Gospels.

source.text: μακάριοι οἱ δοῦλοι ἐκεῖνοι, οὓς ἐλθὼν ὁ κύριος εὑρήσει γρηγοροῦντας· ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι περιζώσεται καὶ ἀνακλινεῖ αὐτοὺς καὶ παρελθὼν διακονήσει αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed the slaves those, whom having come the master will find watching; truly I say to you that he will gird himself and will make recline them and having come up will serve them.

en.L: Blessed [are] those slaves whom the master will find awake when he comes. Truly I tell you that he will gird himself and have them recline [at table], and he will come and serve them.
en.B: Blessed are those servants whom the master finds awake and watching when he comes. Truly I tell you, he will tie on an apron, seat them at the table, and come and wait on them himself.
en.R: How blessed those servants will be if their master finds them awake and ready when he comes! I tell you the truth, the master will put on work clothes himself. He will have the servants sit down to eat, and he will bring them their food.

es.L: Dichosos aquellos esclavos a quienes el señor, al llegar, encuentre velando. En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que se ceñirá, los hará recostarse [a la mesa] y, acercándose, les servirá.
es.B: Dichosos esos siervos a quienes su señor, cuando llegue, encuentre despiertos y alerta. En verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que se pondrá el delantal, los sentará a la mesa y vendrá él mismo a servirles.
es.R: ¡Qué dichosos serán esos siervos si su señor los encuentra despiertos y listos cuando llegue! {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: el señor mismo se pondrá ropa de trabajo. Hará que los siervos se sienten a comer, y él mismo les traerá la comida.

fr.L: Heureux ces esclaves que le maître, à son arrivée, trouvera éveillés. En vérité, je vous dis qu’il se ceindra, les fera se mettre à table et, s’approchant, les servira.
fr.B: Heureux ces serviteurs que le maître, en arrivant, trouvera éveillés et vigilants. En vérité, je vous le dis, il nouera un tablier, les fera asseoir à table et viendra lui-même les servir.
fr.R: Comme ils seront heureux, ces serviteurs, si leur maître les trouve éveillés et prêts quand il arrivera ! Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité : le maître mettra lui-même des vêtements de travail. Il fera asseoir les serviteurs pour manger, et il leur apportera leur nourriture.

sw.L: Heri watumwa wale ambao bwana atakapokuja atawakuta wakikesha. Kweli nawaambia kwamba atajifunga mshipi, na kuwaketisha [mezani], na kuja kuwahudumia.
sw.B: Heri watumishi wale ambao bwana wao atawakuta macho akija. Kweli nawaambia, atajifunga nguo ya kazi, atawaketisha mezani, na yeye mwenyewe atakuja kuwahudumia.
sw.R: Watumishi hao watakuwa na heri kubwa ikiwa bwana wao atawakuta macho na tayari atakapokuja! Nawaambia ukweli, bwana mwenyewe atavaa nguo za kazi. Atawaketisha watumishi wale, naye atawaletea chakula.

vi.L: Phước cho những nô lệ ấy là những người mà khi chủ đến sẽ thấy đang thức canh. Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, chủ sẽ thắt lưng, cho họ ngả mình [dùng bữa], rồi đến phục vụ họ.
vi.B: Phước cho những đầy tớ ấy, khi chủ về thấy họ đang thức canh. Thật vậy, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nói với các con, chủ sẽ thắt lưng, cho họ ngồi vào bàn, rồi tự mình đến dọn ăn cho họ.
vi.R: Những đầy tớ ấy thật có phước khi chủ về thấy họ vẫn thức và sẵn sàng! Ta nói thật với các con, chính người chủ sẽ mặc đồ làm việc. Ông sẽ cho các đầy tớ ngồi vào bàn ăn, rồi đem thức ăn đến phục vụ họ.

ko.L: 주인이 와서 깨어 있는 것을 보게 될 그 종들은 복이 있다. 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 주인이 허리에 띠를 두르고 그들을 [식탁에] 기대어 앉게 하고, 곁에 와서 그들의 시중을 들 것이다.
ko.B: 주인이 돌아와서 깨어 기다리고 있는 것을 보게 될 그 종들은 복이 있다. 진실로 너희에게 말한다. 주인이 앞치마를 두르고 그들을 식탁에 앉힌 다음, 곁에 와서 직접 그들의 시중을 들 것이다.
ko.R: 주인이 돌아왔을 때 깨어서 준비하고 있는 종들은 얼마나 복이 있겠느냐! 내가 분명히 말한다. 주인이 일하는 옷을 입고, 그 종들을 앉혀서 먹게 하고, 그들에게 음식을 가져다줄 것이다.

decisions.choice: slaves: people owned by their master
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for a slave. A slave belonged to the master and lived at his command.

decisions.choice: blessed: fortunate, in a happy state because of God's favor
decisions.reason: The word is the one of the beatitudes (6:20).

decisions.choice: he will gird himself and serve them: the master takes a slave's place
alternatives: he will reward them with money
decisions.reason: Normally slaves served their master at table (17:7-8). Here the master puts on work clothes and serves them. Jesus says he is among his disciples as one who serves (22:27), and in John 13:4-5 he ties a towel around himself and washes their feet.

decisions.choice: recline: lie on couches at a meal
decisions.reason: At a feast guests lay on their side on couches around a low table.

decisions.choice: watching: awake, alert
decisions.reason: The verb means to stay awake and on guard.

decisions.choice: Truly I tell you (L, B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: Luke's usual rendering of Jesus' "amen" (4:24).

decisions.choice: How blessed those servants will be
decisions.reason: Readable makes the declaration an exclamation, as in 6:20.

decisions.choice: tie on an apron
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of dressing for work at table.

decisions.choice: seat them at the table (B); have the servants sit down to eat (R)
decisions.reason: Modern readers sit at meals; the meaning decision explains the custom.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: esclavos (L); siervos (B, R); señor
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice: Literal says what these men were, people owned by their master (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable say "siervos", as the English says "servants". The same through 12:47.

decisions.choice: velando (L); despiertos y alerta (B); despiertos y listos (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for this verb: "velar" at Literal, being awake through the night (meaning decision m5); Balanced and Readable say it in everyday words, as the English says "awake".

decisions.choice: En vérité, je vous le dis (L, B); Je vous le dis, c’est la vérité (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms for Jesus' "amen".

decisions.choice: esclaves (L); serviteurs (B, R); the same for the manager in 12:43-47
decisions.reason: The term sheet's forms, as the English; m1 keeps that they were owned.

decisions.choice: watumwa (L); watumishi (B, R); bwana, lowercase
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice: Literal says what these men were, people owned by their master (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable say "mtumishi", as the English says "servant". The master is the owner in the story, so "bwana" is lowercase. The same through 12:47.

decisions.choice: wakikesha (L); macho (B); macho na tayari (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for this verb: "kukesha" at Literal, staying awake through the night (meaning decision m5); Balanced and Readable say "kuwa macho", awake and alert, as the English says "awake".

decisions.choice: "nô lệ" (L); "đầy tớ" (B, R) for doulos (12:37-47)
decisions.reason: The style guide's forms for doulos: the meaning decision says they were owned by their master, which Literal keeps; Balanced and Readable say "đầy tớ".

decisions.choice: "Thật vậy, Ta nói với các con" (L, B); "Ta nói thật với các con" (R)
decisions.reason: The form settled for "Truly I tell you" in the Gospels; the pronoun takes the setting where it is not at the start of a sentence.

decisions.choice: "종" for doulos at every level, through 12:47
decisions.reason: The Korean style guide has "종" at every level for doulos; it carries both the servant and the slave, and the master serving his slaves is the surprise here.

decisions.choice: "진실로 너희에게 말한다" (L, B); "내가 분명히 말한다" (R) for amēn legō hymin
decisions.reason: As settled for the Korean Gospels.

source.text: κἂν ἐν τῇ δευτέρᾳ κἂν ἐν τῇ τρίτῃ φυλακῇ ἔλθῃ καὶ εὕρῃ οὕτως, μακάριοί εἰσιν ἐκεῖνοι.

records.literal_gloss: And if in the second and if in the third watch he comes and finds thus, blessed are those.

en.L: And if he comes in the second watch, or in the third, and finds [them] so, blessed are those [slaves].
en.B: He may come in the middle of the night or even later, but if he finds them ready, those servants are blessed.
en.R: He may come late at night or in the early hours before dawn. But if he finds them ready, how blessed those servants will be!

es.L: Y si llega en la segunda vigilia, o en la tercera, y [los] encuentra así, dichosos son aquellos [esclavos].
es.B: Puede que llegue a medianoche o aún más tarde, pero si los encuentra preparados, dichosos esos siervos.
es.R: Tal vez llegue tarde en la noche, o de madrugada, antes de que salga el sol. Pero si los encuentra listos, ¡qué dichosos serán esos siervos!

fr.L: Et s’il vient à la deuxième veille, ou à la troisième, et [les] trouve ainsi, heureux sont ces [esclaves].
fr.B: Il viendra peut-être au milieu de la nuit, ou plus tard encore ; mais s’il les trouve prêts, heureux ces serviteurs !
fr.R: Il viendra peut-être tard dans la nuit, ou aux premières heures avant l’aube. Mais s’il les trouve prêts, comme ces serviteurs seront heureux !

sw.L: Na akija katika zamu ya pili ya usiku, au ya tatu, na kuwakuta hivyo, heri wao [watumwa] wale.
sw.B: Huenda akaja usiku wa manane au hata baadaye, lakini akiwakuta wako tayari, heri watumishi hao.
sw.R: Huenda akaja usiku sana, au alfajiri kabla jua halijachomoza. Lakini akiwakuta wako tayari, watumishi hao watakuwa na heri kubwa!

vi.L: Và dù chủ đến vào canh hai, hay vào canh ba, mà thấy họ như vậy, thì phước cho những [nô lệ] ấy.
vi.B: Dù chủ về lúc nửa đêm hay muộn hơn nữa, nếu thấy họ sẵn sàng như vậy, thì những đầy tớ ấy thật có phước.
vi.R: Có thể chủ về lúc khuya, hoặc lúc gần sáng. Nhưng nếu chủ thấy họ vẫn sẵn sàng, những đầy tớ ấy thật có phước!

ko.L: 그리고 주인이 둘째 경에 오든지 셋째 경에 오든지, 그들이 그렇게 하고 있는 것을 보면, 그 [종들은] 복이 있다.
ko.B: 주인이 밤 둘째 경이나 셋째 경에 오더라도, 그들이 그렇게 깨어 있는 것을 보면 그 종들은 복이 있다.
ko.R: 주인이 한밤중에 올 수도 있고, 새벽이 되기 전 늦은 밤에 올 수도 있다. 그래도 주인이 와서 그들이 준비하고 있는 것을 보면, 그 종들은 얼마나 복이 있겠느냐!

decisions.choice: the second and third watch: late in the night, after midnight
decisions.reason: The night was divided into watches, three in Jewish reckoning and four in Roman. Either way, the second and third watches are the dead of night, when it is hardest to stay awake.

decisions.choice: so: awake and ready, as in 12:37
decisions.reason: The word points back to the slaves who watch.

decisions.choice: in the middle of the night or even later (B); late at night or in the early hours before dawn (R)
alternatives: in the second or third watch
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the time in modern terms, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: those servants
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is meant.

decisions.choice: dichosos
decisions.reason: The book-wide word for the Greek (meaning decision m2 at 12:37): fortunate, in a happy state because of God's favor. "Dichoso" says good fortune as well as gladness; "feliz" would say only the feeling.

decisions.choice: heri
decisions.reason: The book-wide word (meaning decision m2 at 12:37): fortunate, in a happy state because of God's favor. "Heri" says good fortune and blessing; "wenye furaha" would say only the feeling.

decisions.choice: zamu ya pili ya usiku, au ya tatu
decisions.reason: The night was divided into watches, here late in the night (meaning decision m1). Swahili counts hours from sunset, so "saa ya pili ya usiku" would mean eight o'clock in the evening; "zamu" (a turn of guard duty) keeps the watch.

decisions.choice: "canh hai", "canh ba" (L)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese counts the watches of the night as "canh", so Literal keeps the Greek count; Balanced and Readable give the time of night (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: "둘째 경 ... 셋째 경" (L, B); "한밤중 ... 새벽이 되기 전 늦은 밤" (R)
decisions.reason: "경" for a watch of the night, as in the Korean Mark 6:48; Readable gives the time of night.

source.text: Τοῦτο δὲ γινώσκετε ὅτι εἰ ᾔδει ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης ποίᾳ ὥρᾳ ὁ κλέπτης ἔρχεται, οὐκ ἂν ἀφῆκεν διορυχθῆναι τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: This however know, that if had known the master of the house in what hour the thief is coming, not he would have allowed to be broken into the house of him.

en.L: But know this: if the master of the house had known in what hour the thief was coming, he would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
en.B: You can be sure of this: if the owner of a house knew the hour when the thief was on his way, he would not let anyone dig through the walls of his house.
en.R: You know that if the owner of a house knew what time a thief was coming, he would not let the thief break into his house.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:sepan|sabed}} esto: que si el dueño de la casa supiera a qué hora viene el ladrón, no dejaría que le perforaran la casa.
es.B: De esto {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} estar seguros: si el dueño de una casa supiera a qué hora va a venir el ladrón, no dejaría que nadie le abriera un boquete en la pared.
es.R: {{plural_you:Ustedes saben|Vosotros sabéis}} que si el dueño de una casa supiera a qué hora va a venir un ladrón, no lo dejaría entrar a robar en su casa.

fr.L: Mais sachez ceci : si le maître de maison avait su à quelle heure le voleur venait, il n’aurait pas laissé percer sa maison.
fr.B: Soyez-en sûrs : si le propriétaire d’une maison savait à quelle heure le voleur va venir, il ne laisserait personne percer les murs de sa maison.
fr.R: Vous le savez : si le propriétaire d’une maison savait à quelle heure un voleur va venir, il ne le laisserait pas entrer de force chez lui.

sw.L: Lakini jueni hili, kwamba kama mwenye nyumba angalijua ni saa gani mwizi anakuja, asingeiacha nyumba yake ivunjwe.
sw.B: Mnaweza kuwa na hakika na hili: kama mwenye nyumba angalijua saa ambayo mwizi angekuja, asingemwacha mtu yeyote atoboe ukuta wa nyumba yake.
sw.R: Mnajua kwamba kama mwenye nyumba angalijua mwizi atakuja saa ngapi, asingemwacha mwizi aingie nyumbani mwake kuiba.

vi.L: Nhưng hãy biết điều này: nếu chủ nhà biết kẻ trộm đến vào giờ nào, thì đã không để nhà mình bị đào ngạch.
vi.B: Các con hãy biết chắc điều này: nếu chủ nhà biết giờ nào kẻ trộm sẽ đến, ông ấy đã không để cho ai đào tường khoét vách nhà mình.
vi.R: Các con biết rằng nếu chủ nhà biết lúc nào kẻ trộm đến, ông ấy sẽ không để kẻ trộm đột nhập vào nhà mình.

ko.L: 그러나 이것을 알아라. 집주인이 도둑이 어느 때에 오는지 알았더라면, 자기 집이 뚫리게 내버려 두지 않았을 것이다.
ko.B: 이것을 알아 두어라. 집주인이 도둑이 몇 시에 올지 알았다면, 도둑이 벽을 뚫고 자기 집에 들어오게 내버려 두지 않았을 것이다.
ko.R: 너희도 알다시피, 집주인이 도둑이 언제 올지 알았다면, 도둑이 자기 집에 들어오지 못하게 했을 것이다.

decisions.choice: he would not have let, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: he would have stayed awake and would not have let
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts have the shorter text. Many others add "he would have stayed awake", which matches Matthew 24:43. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: be broken into: dug through
decisions.reason: The verb means to dig through. Many houses had walls of mud brick, and a thief could dig a hole through them.

decisions.choice: know: a command, "know this"
decisions.reason: The form can be a command or a statement. Either way Jesus appeals to what everyone knows.

decisions.choice: the thief: the unexpected hour of the Son of Man's coming
alternatives: the Son of Man is like a thief in character
decisions.reason: The comparison is about timing only (12:40; 1 Thessalonians 5:2).

decisions.choice: dig through the walls
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of the verb, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: "đào ngạch" (L); "đào tường khoét vách" (B)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 6:19: the thief digs through the wall (meaning decision), which the Vietnamese phrases for a burglar say exactly.

decisions.choice: "뚫리다" (L), "벽을 뚫고" (B)
decisions.reason: The verb is "dug through", as a thief broke through a mud-brick wall; the same picture as the Korean Matthew 6:19.

source.text: καὶ ὑμεῖς γίνεσθε ἕτοιμοι, ὅτι ᾗ ὥρᾳ οὐ δοκεῖτε ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἔρχεται.

records.literal_gloss: Also you be ready, for in the hour not you expect the Son of Man comes.

en.L: You also be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect."
en.B: Be ready yourselves, then. The Son of Man is coming at an hour when you do not think {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will."
